tables.caption: Standardized hospitalization proportion among reported outbreak cases, by pathogen group (12 common-support setting × period cells, pooled-case reference weights). Worst-case intervals are identification intervals, not confidence intervals; bootstrap ranges are the 2.5th–97.5th percentiles of each bound over 2,000 outbreak-level resamples.

Pairwise orderings with their verdict under worst-case bounds and the critical deviation δ*. δ* is the smallest deviation of the unrecorded-status hospitalization rate from the recorded rate at which the δ = 0 ordering is no longer guaranteed (∞, holds with no assumption). Further columns show whether the ordering is determined at δ = 1, 2, 5 and 10 points and the share of bootstrap replicates reproducing the main verdicts.
Robustness analyses, with the number of common-support cells, the number of determined pairwise orderings under worst-case bounds and at δ = 5 points, and changes relative to the main analysis.

Common-support retention by pathogen group, with eligible and retained outbreaks and cases, the settings and periods losing most cases, and crude (unstandardized) proportions before and after the restriction.
Record audit of outbreak outcome fields (C reported cases, H hospitalized, K cases with known hospitalization status), with category counts and handling. No record had a count contradiction.

Outbreak-level bootstrap (2,000 replicates, seed 20261125; outbreaks resampled within group × common-support cell, reference weights recomputed), with the share of replicates giving each verdict and the percentile range of δ* for the main-analysis direction. These describe sampling variability and are not confidence intervals.

Undetermined pairs under worst-case bounds, with the overlap of the two intervals and the group × cell combinations whose unrecorded-status cases contribute most to the interval widths. The decomposition is descriptive and indicates where more complete hospitalization records would narrow the intervals most.

Joint M-estimation statistical inference for the 15 pairwise standardized differences, combining outbreak-cluster HC1 sandwich variance, Imbens–Manski 95% confidence intervals, Gaussian multiplier Max-T stepdown FWER p-values (c = 2.492 worst case; 2.526 at δ = 5 points), and 95% confidence tipping points.

Outbreak-cluster concentration diagnostics across the 12 common-support cells and standard error comparison between stacked M-estimation sandwich estimators (HC0, HC1) and outbreak-level bootstrap (2,000 replicates).

Retrospective masking experiment across 200 Monte Carlo trials on all 2,414 complete-status outbreaks (45,249 cases) in the common support. Values are means (SD) across trials by follow-up case budget.
